title: Frontend: Compress String with Limited Repetition
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Compress String with Limited Repetition. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Implement solution({text,limit}). Return [character,count] runs over Unicode code points, splitting each repeated run into counts <= positive integer limit. Invalid limit throws Invalid limit.
constraints: Define solution(input) in plain JavaScript. Return the documented JSON-compatible value or throw the documented validation error. Each case receives a fresh input.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Scan a maximal equal-character run, then split its count into chunks no larger than the positive integer cap.
alternativeApproaches: Add a decoder and verify round trips for characters that resemble count delimiters.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Long run above cap; exact cap; alternating text.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
